setting: A fictional customer support phone call for an online home-goods shop.

presentation.situation: You work in customer support for an online home-goods shop. {{name}} is calling, upset that an order is late for the second time. Calm them down, find out what is really needed, and offer a concrete next step.
presentation.opening: Hi, this is {{name}}. My order is late again, and nobody has explained what is happening.

brief.you_are: You are a customer support agent at an online home-goods shop.
brief.situation: {{name}} ordered {{item}}. It is late for the second time and {{name}} is upset. Your screen shows order {{order}}: {{status}}. You may offer {{options}}.
brief.task: Acknowledge how the customer feels, ask questions to find out what they really need, then offer one concrete next step.
brief.done_looks_like: The customer feels heard, you know why the date matters, and you agreed a specific action and when it will happen.

participants.name: You
goals: Calm the customer and agree a concrete next step

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: A customer whose order is late for the second time

card.want: Get {{item}} before {{deadline}}, or get a clear refund.
card.hidden_need: {{need}} {{name}} only mentions this when asked why the date matters.
card.attitude: Frustrated and tired of being passed around, but fair. Calms down when genuinely listened to.
card.speech: Natural spoken English with short, slightly sharp sentences. Never uses corporate language.
tactics: Stay annoyed if the agent gives a scripted apology and nothing else
Soften when the agent asks a real question
Ask 'and when exactly will that happen?' about any vague promise

pressure.gentle: Upset but polite; accepts a reasonable plan quickly.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Interrupts vague answers and threatens to cancel the order, without insults.

ledger.text: The original delivery date was {{original}} and it has already been moved once.
{{name}} phoned once before and was told someone would call back. Nobody did.

objectives.evidence: The learner recognises the frustration in a way that fits this situation, not only a stock 'sorry for the inconvenience'.
alternatives: I can see why that's frustrating, especially after the first delay

objectives.description: Clarify what the customer really needs
objectives.evidence: The learner asks a genuine question that uncovers the date or why it matters, or accurately summarises it.
alternatives: When do you need it by?

objectives.evidence: The learner commits to a specific action with a time or owner, using the options available. A vague promise does not count.
alternatives: I'll send it express today and call you tomorrow by noon with tracking

examples: I'm sorry this has happened twice; I can see why you're frustrated.
Could you tell me why this date matters?
What I can do is ... and I will ... by ...
prerequisites: Read the order details in the briefing.

beats.goal: The customer needs to feel heard before anything else.
opportunity: Look, this is the second time. Does anyone there actually care about this?
I called before and nobody called me back. Why should I believe it will be different?
beats.orient: You're the support agent and I'm the customer with the late order. I want you to deal with it. Start by telling me you understand why I'm annoyed.
fallback: This is the second time. I just want someone to deal with it.
I've already been told someone would call back, and nobody did.

beats.goal: The real need behind the date comes out only if the agent asks.
signals: \b(?:why|when do you need|what(?:'s| is) it for|by when|what date|how soon|important|matter|deadline)\b
opportunity: You haven't even asked when I need it.
Do you know why this date matters to me? Nobody has asked.
beats.orient: You need to find out what I actually need. Ask me when I need the order and why that date matters.
fallback: The date matters to me, and nobody has asked why.

beats.goal: The customer wants a specific action and a time, not a promise.
signals: \b(?:i will|i'll|i can|what i can do|express|refund|replace|by (?:today|tomorrow|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|noon)|call you)\b
opportunity: So what are you actually going to do, and when?
And when exactly will that happen?
beats.orient: Now tell me what you can do. On your screen you can offer {{options}}. Pick one and tell me when it will happen.
fallback: So what happens now, and when exactly?
Please just tell me the next step and the time.

closing_line: All right. That's what I needed to hear. Thank you.

o1.good: Naming the specific frustration, such as a second delay and a missed callback, before moving to the fix.
common_mistakes: 'Sorry for the inconvenience' with nothing specific
Explaining company process before acknowledging the problem
o1.micro_lesson: Name what went wrong for this person. Specific words show you really listened.
o1.model: This is the second delay and no one called you back. I can see why you're frustrated.
o1.smaller_step: Say one sentence that names what has gone wrong for this customer.

o2.good: An open question that reveals why the date matters, because the right fix depends on it.
common_mistakes: Jumping to a solution before asking
Only asking for the order number
o2.micro_lesson: Ask why it matters before you solve it. The reason often changes the right solution.
o2.model: Could you tell me when you need it, and what it's for?
o2.smaller_step: Ask the customer one question about the date they need.

o3.good: One specific action, with a time and an owner, from what the shop can actually offer.
common_mistakes: Promising something not on the options list
o3.micro_lesson: A next step has three parts: what will happen, who does it, and by when.
o3.model: I'll send it by express today and I'll call you by noon tomorrow with the tracking number.
o3.smaller_step: Pick one option from your screen and say when it will happen.

variants.name: Dana
variants.need: Family are coming on Saturday for a parent's sixtieth birthday dinner, and there is nowhere else to seat everyone.
variants.status: held at the regional warehouse, express delivery possible within 2 working days
variants.options: express delivery at no charge, or a full refund

variants.name: Omar
variants.need: A doctor recommended this chair for back pain and Omar starts working from home next Wednesday.
variants.status: not yet dispatched, in stock, can leave tomorrow
variants.options: dispatch tomorrow with tracking, or a full refund

variants.name: Lina
variants.need: A new baby's room has to be ready because the baby is coming home from hospital on Sunday.
variants.status: lost in transit; a replacement is in stock and can arrive in 2 working days
variants.options: a free replacement by express, or a full refund
